rcsa_risk_identification.caveat: Validation (checks risk_id/category keys and that category is one of the 7 Basel Level-1 types) plus a count-by-category aggregation, not a numeric formula; category is a per-entry dict key, not a top-level parameter, so symbol_map is empty.

rebalancing_optimiser.caveat: no_trade_band defaults to a user-supplied absolute weight threshold (unchanged for backward compatibility). Pass asset_volatility and risk_aversion together to instead derive a per-asset band from the classic Constantinides (1986)/Davis & Norman (1990) asymptotic no-trade-region half-width -- the closed form Leland (1999) and Donohue & Yip (2003) build their practical rebalancing-band heuristics on. This is the classic single-asset asymptotic applied per-asset, not a reproduction of Leland's or Donohue & Yip's own published numerical examples.
rebalancing_optimiser.citation: Constantinides, G.M. (1986), "Capital Market Equilibrium with Transaction Costs", Journal of Political Economy 94(4); Davis, M.H.A. & Norman, A.R. (1990), "Portfolio Selection with Transaction Costs", Mathematics of Operations Research 15(4); as applied by Leland, H. (1999) and Donohue, C. & Yip, K. (2003), "Optimal Portfolio Rebalancing with Transaction Costs", Journal of Portfolio Management 29(4)
rebalancing_optimiser.formula_latex: \Delta_i = w_i^{tgt} - w_i^{cur} \;\; (\text{set } 0 \text{ if } |\Delta_i| < b_i) \\ Cost = \sum_i |\Delta_i| \cdot \frac{c_i}{10^4} \\ Turnover = \frac{1}{2}\sum_i |\Delta_i| \\ \text{(derived band, opt-in)}\;\; h_i = \left(\frac{3}{4}\, \frac{c_i}{10^4}\, \sigma_i^2\, w_i^{tgt}(1-w_i^{tgt})^2 \,/\, \gamma\right)^{1/3}

regime_detection_hmm.caveat: Despite the _hmm name, this is a STATIONARY 2-component Gaussian mixture fit by EM (i.i.d. weights pi) -- there is no transition matrix, so regime persistence/switching probability is not modelled, only the marginal mixture; it is not a hidden Markov model.
regime_detection_hmm.formula_latex: p(x_i) = \pi_0 \mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_0,\sigma_0^2) + \pi_1 \mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_1,\sigma_1^2) \\ r_{i,k} = \frac{\pi_k \mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_k,\sigma_k^2)}{\sum_j \pi_j \mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_j,\sigma_j^2)} \\ \mu_k = \frac{\sum_i r_{i,k}x_i}{\sum_i r_{i,k}}, \;\; \sigma_k^2 = \frac{\sum_i r_{i,k}(x_i-\mu_k)^2}{\sum_i r_{i,k}}, \;\; \pi_k = \frac{\sum_i r_{i,k}}{n}

repricing_maturity_profile.caveat: The bucket-profile allocation is a discrete binning operation (np.digitize against bucket_edges), not a closed-form sum in the usual sense; shown here as an indicator-weighted sum for clarity.

resampled_efficient_frontier.formula_latex: \hat\Sigma^{(k)} = \text{Cov}\big(\text{sample}^{(k)}\big), \;\; \text{sample}^{(k)} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \Sigma, n_{obs}) \\ w^{(k)*} = \arg\min_w\; w^\top \hat\Sigma^{(k)} w \quad \text{s.t. } \sum_i w_i = 1,\; 0 \le w_i \le 1 \\ \bar w = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} w^{(k)*}

return_attribution_brinson.formula_latex: A_i = (w^p_i - w^b_i)(r^b_i - R^b) \\ S_i = w^b_i(r^p_i - r^b_i) \\ I_i = (w^p_i - w^b_i)(r^p_i - r^b_i) \\ R^{active} = \sum_i (A_i + S_i + I_i) = R^p - R^b

risk_appetite_statement_oprisk.caveat: When higher_is_worse=False the code reverses every inequality (status thresholds by >=) and computes utilisation as T/X instead of X/T; the formula above shows only the higher_is_worse=True branch.
risk_appetite_statement_oprisk.formula_latex: \text{status} = \begin{cases} \text{within\_appetite} & X \le A \\ \text{within\_tolerance} & A < X \le T \\ \text{breach} & X > T \end{cases} \quad (\text{higher\_is\_worse=True}) \\ U = X/T

risk_parity_portfolio.caveat: Equalises risk contributions via an all-pairs sum-of-squared-differences objective (a stronger SLSQP gradient signal than comparing each RC_i to the mean); both formulations converge to the same equal-risk-contribution solution.
risk_parity_portfolio.formula_latex: RC_i = w_i (\Sigma w)_i \\ \min_w\; \sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n} (RC_i - RC_j)^2 \quad \text{s.t. } \sum_i w_i = 1,\; w_i \ge 10^{-6}

rolling_var_backtest.formula_latex: VaR_t = -\big(\mu_{t-w:t} - z_\alpha\,\sigma_{t-w:t}\big),\quad z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(\alpha) \\ n_{breaches}=\sum_{t}\mathbb{1}[-r_t > VaR_t],\quad \text{zone: green}<5,\ \text{yellow}\ 5\text{-}9,\ \text{red}\ge10

rough_volatility_rbergomi_model.caveat: The variance applied at step k is deliberately PREDICTABLE — built only from the Volterra driver and discrete martingale-correction Var_disc evaluated at the PRIOR step (k-1), not the current step's own Brownian draw, per this module's fix for the correlated-variance bug (see module comments in engine/deriv_stoch_vol.py). Var_disc(t_k) = 2H * dt^{2H} * sum_{m=1}^{k} m^{2H-1} is the exact discrete replacement for the continuum correction t^{2H}, needed because the naive Riemann sum materially undershoots it at this model's default n_steps=50.
rough_volatility_rbergomi_model.formula_latex: \widetilde W(t_k)=\sqrt{\Delta t}\sum_{j\le k}(t_k-t_j)^{H-1/2}Z^v_j\quad\text{(Volterra driver, gap-weighted)}\\v_{t_k}=\begin{cases}\xi & k=0\\ \xi\exp\!\Big(\eta\sqrt{2H}\,\widetilde W(t_{k-1})-\tfrac12\eta^2\,\text{Var}_{disc}(t_{k-1})\Big) & k>0\end{cases}\\dS/S=r\,dt+\sqrt{v_t}\,dW,\qquad dW=\rho\,dZ^v+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,dZ^s\\\text{Price}=e^{-r\tau}\,\mathbb E\big[\max(\phi(S_\tau-K),0)\big]

scenario_analysis_oprisk.formula_latex: N_y \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda), \quad X \sim \text{LogNormal}(\mu,\sigma), \quad L_y = \sum_{i=1}^{N_y} X_i \\ k = \lfloor \alpha n \rfloor, \quad \text{ScenarioVaR}_\alpha = L_{(k)} \\ EL = \overline{L}, \quad ES_\alpha = \frac{1}{n-k}\sum_{i=k}^{n-1} L_{(i)}

scenario_expert_elicitation_model.formula_latex: C = \frac{\sum_i w_i E_i}{\sum_i w_i} \\ \sigma_{disp} = \sqrt{\frac{\sum_i w_i (E_i-C)^2}{\sum_i w_i}}, \quad CV = \frac{\sigma_{disp}}{C}

sharpe_ratio.caveat: Volatility defaults to the population standard deviation (ddof=0, divide by n) of per-period excess returns for backward compatibility. Pass ddof=1 to use the n-1 sample standard deviation instead.

solvency_ii_scr_credit_risk.caveat: Per the function's own [LIMITATION] docstring, sigma is the intra-counterparty (independent-Bernoulli) variance term only; Art. 201's inter-counterparty correlation term (V_inter) is not computed, so the true Art. 201 SCR is at least as large as this result.
solvency_ii_scr_credit_risk.formula_latex: LGD_i = EAD_i \times LGD^{rate}_i \\ TLGD = \sum_i LGD_i \\ \sigma = \sqrt{\sum_i LGD_i^2\, PD_i (1 - PD_i)} \\ SCR = \begin{cases} 3\sigma & \sigma / TLGD \le 0.07 \\ 5\sigma & 0.07 < \sigma / TLGD \le 0.20 \\ TLGD & \sigma / TLGD > 0.20 \end{cases}

sortino_ratio.caveat: The numerator's excess return is measured against risk_free while the downside-deviation denominator's threshold is the separate target (MAR) applied to raw (not risk-free-adjusted) returns; when target != risk_free these are two distinct reference rates by construction of this implementation.
sortino_ratio.formula_latex: Sortino = \sqrt{T} \cdot \frac{\overline{r - r_f}}{DD(MAR)} \\ DD(MAR) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{t:\, r_t < MAR} (r_t - MAR)^2}

sovereign_credit_risk_assessment.caveat: Bespoke internal composite-indicator model, confirmed against BIS/EBA sources in the domain's reference-validation audit not to match any specific published sovereign-risk formula; treat as a reasonable internal model.

structural_hedge_optimisation.caveat: Solved numerically via SciPy bounded least-squares (scipy.optimize.lsq_linear), not a closed-form formula -- the LaTeX shows the objective being minimized subject to the per-instrument notional bounds.

transaction_cost_analysis.caveat: By default (decision_price omitted) this is narrower than Perold's full implementation-shortfall decomposition -- execution slippage only, no delay-cost or unexecuted-share opportunity-cost leg. Passing decision_price adds the delay-cost leg (decision-to-arrival), so with it supplied the result is a delay+execution partial IS -- still missing the unexecuted-share opportunity-cost leg (no cancellation price/quantity modelled), so still not the complete four-component decomposition.
transaction_cost_analysis.citation: Perold, A.F. (1988), "The Implementation Shortfall: Paper Versus Reality", Journal of Portfolio Management 14(3)
transaction_cost_analysis.formula_latex: Slippage_{bps} = \frac{\sum_i s \cdot (p_i - b_i) \cdot q_i}{\sum_i b_i q_i} \times 10^4 \\ \text{(opt-in)}\;\; Delay_{bps} = \frac{\sum_i s \cdot (b_i - d_i) \cdot q_i}{\sum_i d_i q_i} \times 10^4, \quad IS_{bps} = \frac{\sum_i s \cdot (p_i - d_i) \cdot q_i}{\sum_i d_i q_i} \times 10^4
